summary: Iran launched missile attacks from its territory toward Aqaba, Jordan, with potential spillover into southern Israel prompting interceptor launches. Kuwait suffered repeated attacks on a power and desalination plant, causing fire and outages. The IRGC Navy declared the Strait of Hormuz will remain blocked amid continued US-Iran hostilities.
key_points: Iran fired missiles toward Aqaba, Jordan, with Israeli officials warning fragments could fall in southern Israel and launching interceptors over Eilat (Source: @inon_yttach/9527).
Kuwait's electricity ministry said a power and desalination plant was attacked for the second time in two days, catching fire and taking units offline (Source: @kianmeli1/89636).
IRGC Navy stated the Strait of Hormuz will remain blocked as long as 'US mischief' continues, with vessels met by Iranian response (Source: @Faytuks_Network/5173).
US and Israeli interceptor systems engaged Iranian missiles to Aqaba; Iron Dome interceptors launched at fragments near Eilat with no damage (Source: @New_security8200/202765).
A Hezbollah drone-operating cell was spotted by IDF Commando Brigade near Kfar Tebnit and killed by IAF strikes in southern Lebanon (Source: @manniefabian/58803).
US Embassy in Jordan said Aqaba airport and port were evacuated due to a specific threat following Iranian launches (Source: @inon_yttach/9523).
Explosions were reported at Langa port and Arak city, where a previously struck plutonium reactor is located, in Iran (Source: @New_security8200/202751).
Israel suspended all flights at Ramon Airport north of Eilat following regional attacks and Aqaba targeting (Source: @kianmeli1/89640).

sections.executive_summary: Iran launched missiles from its territory toward Aqaba, Jordan, with Israeli and US interceptors engaged to prevent fragment fallout in Eilat. Kuwait's power and desalination plant was struck for the second time in two days, causing fire and unit outages. The IRGC Navy declared the Strait of Hormuz will remain blocked while US-Iran hostilities continue across the region.

sections.threat_assessment: Iran's missile launches at Aqaba and repeated strikes on Kuwaiti energy infrastructure demonstrate widening reach beyond Israel, risking Gulf supply chains. IRGC Navy's Hormuz blockade threat directly endangers commercial shipping and US forces. Hezbollah drone activity in southern Lebanon shows continued border probing against IDF troops. US troop deaths in Jordan and interceptor engagements signal potential for direct US-Iran confrontation across the region.
sections.regional_response: US published renewed global travel warning and moved dozens of fuel aircraft to Israel while evacuating Aqaba port with Jordan after specific threats. Israel suspended Ramon Airport flights and considers civilian drone ban amid escalation fears. Kuwait's ministry confirmed plant attacks but messages show no stated Gulf military response. Yemeni source via al-Mayadeen warned Saudi targets are within reach, indicating broader axis mobilization risk.
sections.intelligence_notes: Open-source Telegram channels show fragmented but concurrent attack patterns: Iran-to-Jordan missiles, Kuwait energy hits, and Iranian internal explosion reports. Israeli and US interceptors operated jointly over Aqaba, revealing coordinated air defense. Claims of Khamenei son's absence and IRGC message control are single-source and unverified. Execution of Iranian protesters and drone shootdowns suggest internal and external pressure converging on the regime.
